---
title: "quartoReactive — Phase 2 Demo"
format: html
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(quartoReactive)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
```

## Define Data + Filters

```{r}
#| include: false
interactive_df <- interactive_df(mtcars) |>
  filter_on("cyl",  input = "radio", label = "Cylinders", show_all = TRUE) |>
  filter_on("gear", input = "dropdown", label = "Gears") |>
  filter_on("am",   input = "radio", label = "Transmission")
```

## Filters

```{r}
render_inputs(interactive_df)
```

## Scatter Plot

```{r}
reactive(plot_ly(interactive_df, x = ~mpg, y = ~hp, color = ~factor(cyl),
                 type = "scatter", mode = "markers"))
```

## Data Table

```{r}
reactive(datatable(interactive_df[, c("mpg", "cyl", "disp", "hp", "wt", "gear", "am")]))
```

## How It Works

1. `interactive_df(mtcars)` creates a data.frame subclass carrying reactive metadata
2. `filter_on()` declares filters without rendering them
3. `render_inputs()` places the filter controls in the document
4. `reactive(plot_ly(...))` wraps plotly and connects it to the data store
5. `reactive(datatable(...))` wraps DT and connects it to the same store

All filtering happens **client-side in the browser**. No server needed.
Both widgets update simultaneously when any filter changes.
